tagline.en: Who did it, or what happened to it?
tagline.bn: কে করল, নাকি কী করা হলো?

subtitle.en: Every card has a short rule and 3 questions. See how “Ali broke the window” becomes “The window was broken”, in every tense you know.
subtitle.bn: প্রতিটি কার্ডে ছোট্ট নিয়ম আর ৩টি প্রশ্ন। দেখো কীভাবে “Ali broke the window” হয়ে যায় “The window was broken”, সব tense-এ।

hint.en: Doer first, or the thing first?
When to say who did it

cards.badge: Ali broke it → It was broken

rule.en: In the active voice, the doer comes first (Ali broke the window). In the passive voice, the thing that the action happens to comes first (The window was broken).
rule.bn: Active voice-এ কর্তা আগে আসে। Passive voice-এ যার উপর কাজটি হয়েছে, সেটি আগে আসে।

recap.example: Active: Mum cooks dinner. · Passive: Dinner is cooked by Mum.

options.why: The doer (Ali) comes first, so this is active.
Ali is the doer and comes first: active.

options.text: The window was broken by Ali.

options.why: There is no “be + past participle” here, so it is not passive.

questions.explanation: The window comes first and the verb is was + broken (be + past participle): passive.

options.why: is + cooked is passive. The dinner comes first.
was + cooked is passive, and the doer is not even named.
has been + cooked is passive.

questions.explanation: The doer (Mum) comes first and does the action: active.

questions.prompt: In “The cake was eaten by the children”, who did the eating?

options.why: The cake didn’t eat anything. It was eaten.
Someone did eat it: the person after “by”.
Only the children did the action. The cake had it done to it.

questions.explanation: The doer comes after “by”: the children.

rule.en: Every passive verb has a form of “be” (am, is, are, was, were, been, be) plus the past participle (V3: written, made, eaten).
rule.bn: প্রতিটি passive verb-এ থাকে “be”-এর একটি রূপ (am, is, are, was, were, been, be) + past participle (V3)।

recap.example: is made · was written · will be sent

options.why: “Wrote” is the past (V2). The passive needs the past participle: written.
“Is” is present, but “yesterday” is past.
A letter can’t write. It needs the passive: was written.

questions.explanation: Past passive: was + written (V3).

options.text: a form of be + a past participle

options.why: That is the simple future, not the passive.
-ing alone is not passive.
That is for questions and negatives in the present.

questions.explanation: That is the passive formula: be + V3.

questions.prompt: What is the past participle (V3) of “speak”?

options.why: “Spoke” is the past (V2), not the past participle.
“Speak” is irregular. There is no “speaked”.
“Speaking” is the -ing form, not the past participle.

questions.explanation: speak → spoke → spoken. The passive uses V3: spoken.

rule.en: For facts and habits: am, is or are + past participle.
rule.bn: সত্য ঘটনা বা অভ্যাস বোঝাতে: am / is / are + past participle।

options.why: After “is”, the passive needs the past participle: spoken.
English is one thing, so use is.
A language can’t speak. It is spoken.

questions.explanation: English is one language: is + spoken.

options.why: “Toys” are many, so use are.
After “are”, use the past participle: made.
It needs “are” before made: are made.

questions.explanation: Many toys: are + made.

questions.prompt: “They clean the room every day.” → “The room ___ every day.”

options.why: A room can’t clean. It is cleaned.
“Clean” here is a describing word. The passive needs “cleaned”.
The room is one, so use is.

questions.explanation: The room (one) + is + cleaned (V3).

rule.en: For finished past actions: was or were + past participle.
rule.bn: শেষ হয়ে যাওয়া অতীতের কাজে: was / were + past participle।

options.why: After “was”, use the past participle: built.
One bridge takes was, not were.
A bridge can’t build. It needs was: was built.

questions.explanation: One bridge, in the past: was + built.

questions.prompt: The thieves ___ by the police last night.

options.why: “Thieves” are many, so use were.
After “were”, use the past participle: caught.
Without “were”, it sounds like the thieves did the catching.

questions.explanation: Many thieves, in the past: were + caught.

questions.prompt: “Rabindranath Tagore wrote Gitanjali.” → “Gitanjali ___ by Rabindranath Tagore.”

options.why: The active sentence is past, so the passive is past too: was written.
“Wrote” is V2. Use the past participle: written.
A book can’t write. It was written.

questions.explanation: Past tense becomes was + written.

rule.en: For something done before now: has or have + been + past participle.
rule.bn: এখনকার আগে যা করা হয়েছে: has / have + been + past participle।

options.why: “The homework” is one thing (it), so use has.
Without “been”, it means the homework did something.
After “has”, use been, not being.

questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: has + been + done.

questions.prompt: Three new schools ___ in our town.

options.why: “Schools” are many, so use have.
Schools can’t build. It needs been: have been built.
After “been”, use the past participle: built.

questions.explanation: Many schools: have + been + built.

options.why: A bike can’t steal. It has been stolen.
“Stole” is V2. Use the past participle: stolen.
One bike takes has, not have.

questions.explanation: One bike: has + been + stolen.

rule.en: For the future: will + be + past participle. “Be” never changes.
rule.bn: ভবিষ্যতের জন্য: will + be + past participle। “be” কখনো বদলায় না।

recap.example: The results will be announced tomorrow.

options.why: You need “be” between will and the past participle.
After “be”, use the past participle: announced.
This is not English. Use “will be announced”.

questions.explanation: Future passive: will + be + announced.

options.why: You need “be”: will be held.
After “be”, use the past participle: held.
This is not English. Use “will be held”.

questions.explanation: Future passive: will + be + held (V3 of hold).

questions.prompt: “The teacher will check the tests.” → “The tests ___ by the teacher.”

options.why: Tests can’t check. They will be checked.
After “be”, use the past participle: checked.
You need “be”: will be checked.

questions.explanation: will + be + checked.

rule.en: For something happening at that moment: am, is, are, was or were + being + past participle.
rule.bn: যে কাজ সেই মুহূর্তে চলছে: am / is / are / was / were + being + past participle।

options.why: This is for facts or habits. “Right now” needs “is being repaired”.
After “is”, use being, not been.
After “being”, use the past participle: repaired.

questions.explanation: “Right now” + passive: is + being + repaired.

options.why: After “being”, use the past participle: cooked.
“Dinner” is one thing, so use was.
After “was”, use being, not been.

questions.explanation: In progress at a past moment: was + being + cooked.

questions.prompt: The new classrooms ___ painted this week.

options.why: “Classrooms” are many, so use are.
After “are”, use being, not been.
It needs “are” before being.

questions.explanation: Many classrooms, in progress now: are + being + painted.

rule.en: Add “by + doer” only when it matters who did it. Leave it out when the doer is unknown, obvious or not important.
rule.bn: কে করেছে তা জরুরি হলে “by + কর্তা” যোগ করো। কর্তা অজানা, স্পষ্ট বা অগুরুত্বপূর্ণ হলে বাদ দাও।

recap.example: The song was sung by Rina. · My wallet was stolen.

questions.prompt: The Mona Lisa was painted ___ Leonardo da Vinci.

options.why: “With” is for a tool: painted with a brush.
“From” shows where something comes from, not who did it.
“For” shows who something is meant for.

questions.explanation: In the passive, the doer comes after by.

questions.prompt: When can you leave out “by + doer”?

options.why: You can leave it out. “My bike was stolen” is a full, correct sentence.
It can be left out in any kind of sentence.

options.text: When the doer is unknown or not important

options.why: It can be left out in any tense.

questions.explanation: If we don’t know or don’t need to say who did it, we leave it out: My bike was stolen.

options.text: The poem was written with my sister.
options.why: “With” means together with, or a tool. The doer needs by.

options.text: The poem was written by my sister.
The poem was written from my sister.
options.why: “From” shows where something came from.

options.text: The poem was written of my sister.
options.why: “Of” doesn’t show the doer. Use by.

questions.explanation: by + the doer (my sister).
